Context epochs

  session 5d1a2b3c-4e5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d  ·  2 epochs
    first recorded 2026-08-10 20:25:04 UTC
    1  opened by startup, ended by a context reset
       9 tool calls, 1 turn with work, 2 calls by a subagent
    2  opened by compact, ended with the session (other)
       2 tool calls, 1 turn with work

A context epoch is the work recorded for one session identity between the
points where the agent reported starting a context. Compaction was observed
starting one under the same identity; /clear was observed ending a session
and starting the next under a different one. Axiom never links two
identities: where one appears after another here, that is the order they
were recorded in and nothing more.

A turn can span a context reset, so turns with work are counted inside each
epoch and do not add up to a session total.

Observed harness provenance

  session 5d1a2b3c-4e5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
    session starts 1, 2, same observed components
      CLAUDE.md                       observed  3f786850e387…
      .claude/settings.json           nothing found there
      .claude/settings.local.json     observed  89e6c98d9288…
      .claude/agents                  enumerated, 1 definition
        explore.md                    observed  b3a8e0e1f9ab…

Harness provenance is what Axiom looked at for itself when a session start
was recorded, at the project root it resolved from that session's working
directory. It is a record of those exact paths at that moment and nothing
else. Contents are never recorded: a digest is a SHA-256 of a file's exact
bytes, taken with no normalization, and one byte of difference makes a
different digest. A path that is a link is read only where it leads to a file
inside the project, and where a link led is never recorded.

It is not the configuration Claude Code loaded. Axiom does not observe user,
enterprise or command-line configuration, a file reached through an import,
plugins, skills, MCP servers, the model, or anything else the agent was
given, and only the top level of the definitions directory is enumerated.
Components that match establish that these paths held the same bytes: not
that two sessions ran under the same harness, and nothing whatever about how
either one behaved.

A recorded turn is a turn identifier at least one recorded tool call named.
A turn is the context an agent labels with an identifier of its own: it is
not established to be one request, one task, or one complete unit of work.
Identifiers carried only by a session start or end, or only by a usage
record, named no recorded work and are not listed, because a turn built from
one would be a turn that did nothing. Turns are numbered within a session
identity, in the order their work was recorded, and an identifier means
nothing outside the session that issued it.

The time beside a turn is the earliest and latest recorded on its calls. It
is not how long the turn took, and nothing above is ordered by it:
membership and order come from the order records were appended.

Subagent launches counts calls that handed work to a nested agent, and
calls by a nested agent counts the work one did. Neither is derived from
the other, and adding them together counts nothing meaningful: a launch
reported failing started no agent, a launch whose outcome was not recorded
settles nothing either way, and nested calls appear with no launch beside
them whenever the log begins after one was already running.

A launch listed under a turn is one the agent returned an agent identity
for, and the work under it is the recorded calls that reported that same
identity. That is the whole claim. It does not establish that everything
the agent did reached the log, that it finished what it was asked, or
anything about what it consumed, and these counts are not a breakdown of
calls by a nested agent above: that counts every nested call, including
work no recorded launch accounts for.

1 recorded tool call named no turn, so they appear in no turn above.

Read across related agent scopes

  /repo/calc/calc.go
      session 5d1a2b3c-4e5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
      the session scope and the agents it launched
        the session scope, 3 reads
        agent 1, 1 read

  /repo/strutil/strutil.go
      session 5d1a2b3c-4e5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
      the session scope and the agents it launched
        the session scope, 1 read
        agent 2, 1 read

2 paths read in more than one related agent scope.

A path is listed where a successful whole-file read of it was recorded in
more than one agent scope, and a recorded launch relates those scopes. That
is what it says. It does not say that either agent held what the other read,
that one reading stood in for the other, or that anything about how the work
was handed over follows from it.

Scopes are related only through a launch whose record carried the agent
identity it returned. A launch with no identity recorded relates nothing,
and a nested agent whose identity no recorded launch returned takes part in
no group. Timing, proximity, turn identifiers and tool names take no part in
any of it.

A group is one launching scope together with the scopes it launched
directly. The relation is followed no further: a group holding every agent
of a session would say nothing about why two scopes appear side by side.
Two agents launched by one scope are compared; an agent and the scope that
launched its launcher are not.

Nothing here is an ordering. A nested agent's work reaches the log before
the launch that names it as often as after, so the section says a path was
read in more than one related scope and never which read came first.

Paths are compared as the exact strings the agent recorded. Two spellings of
one file stay apart, which can lose a relation and never invent one.

The session scope is the work recorded under no agent identity. A numbered
agent is one nested identity, numbered within its session in the order the
log first mentions it: the numbering is Axiom's own, and it names no agent
outside this report.

Read again in a later context epoch

  /repo/calc/calc.go
      session 5d1a2b3c-4e5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
      epoch 1, opened by startup, 2 reads, no later write or edit recorded
      epoch 2, opened by compact, 1 read, later write or edit recorded

1 path read in more than one context epoch.

A path is listed where a whole-file read of it succeeded in more than one
context epoch of one session identity. That is an observed ordering of reads
around a recorded boundary, and nothing more: an epoch boundary is a
structural boundary in the log, not proof that the agent's context was
discarded, and an epoch also ends where a session does, which discards
nothing.

Boundaries are recorded only where the agent reported one, so they are a
lower bound: a boundary Axiom did not observe leaves the reads on either
side of it looking like one epoch, and no relation is reported.

Where a write or edit of the same path was recorded after the read in that
epoch, the line says so. It is an ordering of two recorded operations. It
does not say the file changed, because a call the agent reported failing was
still a call that was recorded, and it does not say why the read happened.
Where none was recorded, that is not evidence the read achieved nothing.

Session identities are never compared. Nothing recorded links one to
another, so a path read under two of them appears here under neither.

A nested agent reasons in a context of its own, and these epochs are the
session's, so its reads are not part of this. 2 successful whole-file reads
were set aside.

Observed operations

  File              7   read, written or edited; attributed by path below
  Shell             1   effects not observable; never attributed
  Subagent          2   the nested agent's calls are recorded separately
  Unrecognized      1   Axiom cannot say what these did

Each observed tool call is counted once above, and a call rejected before it
ran is never recorded at all. Only a file operation names a path, so only
those are attributed below; the rest is work Axiom either cannot attribute
to a path or cannot interpret at all.

Work by path, under /repo

  calc/calc.go
      4 reads, 1 modification, 2 turns, 58ms
  strutil/strutil.go
      2 reads, 1 turn, 14ms

Every file operation observed at a path is counted: reads of a whole file,
ranged reads of part of one, writes and edits, and operations that failed. A
category with none observed is left out of a path's line. Time is the sum of
the durations the agent reported for those operations, not elapsed time. A
dash means Axiom recorded nothing complete; it never means zero.

The lines above describe the 7 of 11 observed tool calls that named a path.

No read was measured, so no path reports read bytes. Sizes are recorded only
while a receiver is running, which is not an absence of bytes.

Findings

  Repeated file read                         session 5d1a2b3c
    Read 2 times, with no agent modification observed in between
    Potentially redundant reads       1
    Repeated-call tool time           7ms
    File                              /repo/calc/calc.go
    Window                            2026-08-10 20:25:09 → 20:25:11 UTC

1 finding.

Repeated-call tool time is how long the repeated calls took to execute, not
counting the first. It is not the total time of the operation, and it
measures nothing about context, tokens, or cost. Axiom reports what it
observed; a file may still have been changed by something outside the agent.
